before.title: Primary timing measures complete SQL round trips
before.subtitle: Frontend command arrival → complete response delivery; summed per application request
before.source: Source: RTT_MEASUREMENT_PLAN.md; METHODS.md; compact collector sources and per-request RTT records
paragraphs: Compact protocol collectors record complete exchanges at 0 / 2 / 10 ms added database-response delay. Every primary request supplies both its summed SQL round-trip time and its actual command counts.

The boundary includes database execution and response transfer. Application computation between calls stays outside. All request-owned connections contribute, including native identity lookups; a WeBridge CALL is counted once.

Compilers, profilers and timing runs share an exclusive host lease. Complete returned results and final committed state gate the measured values. Separate deep profiles retain nested SQL; application and database-server timings retain their own scopes.

after.title: The remaining feed SELECT accounts for measured server work
after.subtitle: Same secondary +2 ms rich-trace diagnostic; conventional Java and its generated procedure
after.source: Source: profiles/paged-feed-cost-analysis/EXPLANATION.md; mysql-request-rows.json; SELECT event IDs and generated SQL in the retained profiles
paragraphs: Conventional Java executes one business SELECT per feed page. WeBridge moves that SELECT into CALL and reduces five complete client exchanges to three.
The SELECT takes a median 34.1725 ms directly and 33.7765 ms inside the procedure; it returns 20 rows and examines a median 20,110 rows. Two setup commands remain outside CALL.

The pruned graph form retains three wrapped top-K SELECTs: seven client exchanges become three, while inclusive server work remains about 174 ms. The profile distinguishes query work from command bundling.

after.title: Source-faithful money handling exposes a numerical model boundary
after.subtitle: Observed NewOrder synthesis failures and bad-credit Payment installation failures
after.source: Source: tpcc/numeric-model-boundary.json; tpcc/stage-failures.json; case-linked original symbolicBigDecimal.cpp and SPParser diagnostics
paragraphs: The Java port preserves Python's round(float, 2) through BigDecimal(double) and HALF_EVEN. Native symbolic replay reaches scales 45–47 before setScale(2).
The symbolic model forms a long divisor from pow(10, scale difference); the observed expression contains -9223372036854775808. The source model also leaves the rounding-mode argument unused.

NewOrder's emitted symbolic expression fails Java-expression parsing. Bad-credit Payment emits the expression as a procedure formal parameter and MySQL rejects installation. Exact stage artifacts identify each affected case.

after.title: What the evidence bundle preserves
after.subtitle: Re-run scripts, per-request observations, independent oracles and source identities
after.source: Source: PUBLIC_FILES manifests; archive-manifest.json; verify_archive.py; results.json
paragraphs: Every reported cell points to raw request timings or a concrete compiler-stage failure, plus its fixture reset, effective settings and correctness receipts.
SQL/protocol profiles retain command text, complete response ordering, actual procedure activation, server statement events and explicit category totals.
Large identical state payloads share one gzip object through relative links. The archive ledger verifies the original uncompressed bytes, stored object hashes and each logical evidence path.
